body: `parseNewLines` advances `lastFileOffset` to `fileSize` even when `newContent` does not end with a newline. If the rollout JSONL is being appended and the last line is incomplete, the JSON parse will fail and that partial line will be skipped permanently on the next incremental read. Consider buffering the trailing partial line and only advancing the offset to the last complete newline boundary.

`inferStatus` creates new `ISO8601DateFormatter` instances for every parsed line. This can be a hot path (called every 3s and iterating many JSONL lines) and formatters are expensive to instantiate. Consider caching one/two shared formatters (fractional + non-fractional) as static properties and reusing them.

`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` is changed to `GT2SGCCN5R` for the app target, while the project Release configuration still uses `2DKS5U9LV4`. Committing a specific team ID (and having inconsistent team IDs between project/target configs) can break code signing for other developers/CI. Consider removing hard-coded team IDs from the project file (or moving them to user/CI-specific xcconfig) and ensuring project/target configs are consistent.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Consume cached tool_use_id when binding permission requests**

This path now only peeks a cached `tool_use_id` for response-required events and defers cache consumption to `PostToolUse`, which means denied approvals (where `PostToolUse` usually never arrives) leave the old ID in the queue. The next matching approval request can then reuse that stale ID, causing separate approvals to collapse onto one interaction identifier; downstream projection logic upserts approvals by ID, so later requests can overwrite prior approval state and make command targeting ambiguous.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Deduplicate detected Codex sessions by variant as well as ID**

Session discovery deduplicates on `sessionId` before preserving whether the process is CLI or App. With the new split adapters (`codex-cli` vs `codex-app`), two active Codex processes in the same cwd can resolve to the same session ID, so whichever one is parsed first suppresses the other; after adapter-specific variant filtering, one live runtime can disappear from discovery entirely, which breaks visibility and control for that session.

When piping `xcodebuild` into `xcpretty`, the script can incorrectly succeed even if `xcodebuild` fails because `set -e` alone does not propagate failures through pipelines. Consider enabling `set -o pipefail` (or `set -euo pipefail`) near the top, or otherwise capturing `xcodebuild`’s exit status so build failures aren’t masked when `xcpretty` is installed.

`ClaudeCrabIcon.animateLegs` is still part of the API and is set in the initializer, but it’s no longer used to influence rendering/animation (the icon rotates unconditionally). This makes call sites like `ClaudeCrabIcon(..., animateLegs: isAnyProcessing)` misleading. Either wire `animateLegs` into the new animation behavior (e.g., only rotate when true / change speed) or remove the parameter to avoid dead API surface.

The bundled hook now unconditionally auto-allows every `PermissionRequest` and exits immediately. This removes the user consent gate that Claude Code’s permission system provides and could allow unintended tool actions. Consider making this behavior opt-in (e.g., behind a setting / env var) and ensure the UI and documentation clearly communicate the security implications.

`GhosttyController.focusSession`/`enumerateTerminals` executes AppleScript synchronously (noted as ~400ms) and is called from `@MainActor` code paths. This can block the main run loop and cause visible UI hangs when the hotkey/click is used. Consider moving AppleScript execution onto a dedicated serial background queue (still serialized for NSAppleScript safety) and only hopping back to the main actor for UI-affecting calls, or otherwise making the focus path async without blocking the main thread.

`focus(_:)` acknowledges the session before attempting any activation. If Ghostty focus fails and no known terminal app is running (or activation is denied), the session will still be marked acknowledged and its checkmark will disappear even though the user wasn’t actually taken to the session. Consider only acknowledging after a successful focus/activation result, or re-arming the acknowledgment when all focus strategies fail.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Register a default profile when profile is missing**

Usage tracking is gated behind `if let profile = event.profile`, so sessions only get registered with `UsageTracker` when hooks explicitly send a profile. In the current flow the installed hook command still runs without `--profile`, and the Python hook omits `profile` in that case, which means default-profile users never populate `profileUsage` and won’t see the new usage bars/history unless they manually patch their hook config.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute lifetime savings after plan changes**

This block only computes lifetime savings for profiles that are not already cached, so once a profile is initialized, changing its plan override later does not refresh `totalSubscriptionCost`. The UI can then continue showing stale lifetime savings based on the previous monthly fee, which is incorrect for the settings-driven plan override workflow introduced in this change.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse subscription dates without requiring fractional seconds**

The ISO-8601 parser is configured with `.withFractionalSeconds`, which fails on valid timestamps like `2026-04-01T12:00:00Z` that omit fractional seconds. When parsing fails, downstream code falls back to `months = 1`, materially skewing lifetime subscription-cost and savings calculations for older accounts.
